text: User documentation published in 2ab52e8. docs/tutorial/ is a seven-step task path -- first plot, scales and guides, statistics, facets and coordinates, themes and styling, composition, saving output -- taking a reader from a case class to a file on disk, so the criterion 'create, customize, combine, display and save plots from task-oriented guides' is met end to end. docs/gallery.md holds ten plates (scatter, line, histogram, density, summary intervals, ribbon, heatmap, contour, facet panels, one composed figure); each is a compiled program followed by intaglio.docs.Gallery writing that program's render to docs/gallery/<plate>.svg and returning the image link, so the gallery's source sits directly above its generated output and both are one artifact in version control. Because SVG is text, the plates are diffable, and tools/check-docs.sh re-renders them and fails when a committed file differs -- the gallery is a regression court as well as a document. docs/backends.md compares the six backends and what each can and cannot express; docs/limits.md covers the deterministic performance gates, the hard limits and the golden and fuzz courts, quoting performance/baselines/v1.tsv verbatim; docs/notebooks.md covers the Jupyter MIME-bundle route and publication; docs/accessibility.md gained the per-grob metadata section. Versioned and executable: the guides live in the repository under version control, mdoc substitutes @VERSION@ from the build, and every fenced 'mdoc' block is compiled -- 48 documents, 136 checked fences, 0 errors. docs/README.md indexes all of it and the README now opens onto it. Not established: no documentation site is built or deployed, so 'publish' means published in the repository; a reader gets the guides from GitHub, not from a versioned site with an API cross-link. The Scaladoc apiURL points at a Pages URL that does not exist yet. The composed-figure plate renders correctly but is visually tight at the gallery's fixed 560x360 canvas.
